best_for: Windows users cleaning up a cluttered PC or a fresh laptop full of preinstalled apps, who want to tick twenty programs and remove them in one pass instead of clicking through twenty uninstallers.
description:
Bulk Crap Uninstaller, BCU for short, is a program manager published under the name Marcin Szeniak; the project site says it is maintained by Klocman. It is translated into more than a dozen languages, including Spanish, German, French, Polish and Brazilian Portuguese.

When you know the app but not its name, you can point BCU at a window, a shortcut or a folder and remove whatever it belongs to. It copes with uninstallers that crash or hang. BCU can verify uninstaller certificates and shows ratings for apps, and you can filter the list with presets or your own regex rules, then export it. You can also set commands to run before and after each removal.

points.title: Bulk removal with few prompts
points.text: Pick many programs and BCUninstaller runs their uninstallers one after another, quietly where it can. It can even make some uninstallers that lack a silent mode run without asking, so a long list clears while you do something else.

points.title: Finds more than the Apps list shows
points.text: Besides normal installs it detects hidden entries, apps whose uninstaller is missing, portable apps, Steam and Oculus games, Chocolatey packages, Microsoft Store apps, Windows Features and Windows Updates.

points.title: Cleans up what uninstallers leave
points.text: After removal it searches for leftover files and registry entries and clears empty folders from Program Files. Review what it finds before you delete; a force uninstall skips the app's own uninstaller and can leave services or registrations behind.

points.title: Free for home and work
points.text: BCUninstaller is open source under the Apache 2.0 license and free for private and commercial use. It also has a startup manager and a command-line mode for scripted removals.

points.title: Version 6 wants Windows 10
points.text: The 6.x line targets Windows 10 and later and needs the .NET 8 desktop runtime, which the setup adds if missing. The portable build bundles its own runtime. On Windows 7 SP1 use the 5.x line, which ends at 5.9.

points.title: Windows only, 18 versions kept
points.text: There is no macOS or Linux version. The Windows listing keeps 18 versions of the machine-wide setup, back to 4.16, so the 5.9 build for Windows 7 is still here if 6.x will not run.
